Subject: Split-DNS stub zones & gateway TLS termination — action items for Acme deployment

Hi team,

Thanks again for the deep dive earlier. I took notes on the DNS and TLS pieces we discussed and wanted to put a concrete set of options and next steps in writing so we can converge quickly. Attaching a stubzone-mapping.xlsx that contains the hostnames we've been iterating on.

High-level options (summary):
- Option A: Terminate TLS at Acme edge (your reverse proxy). Redwood sees requests over a private peering/VPN; DNS uses a split-stub zone that maps private hostnames to the peering endpoints.
- Option B: Terminate TLS at Redwood private endpoint, with mutual TLS (mTLS) between Acme edge and Redwood. Requires customer to accept Redwood CA or use client certs.

Questions for decision:
1) Which termination option do you prefer? (A or B)
2) For Option A: will Acme use ACME (Let's Encrypt/your internal ACME) or provide a wildcard SAN cert?
3) For Option B: can Acme accept our CSR process and HSM-backed key management, or do you require offline key generation?

Operational asks (short):
- Please confirm the internal zone name you want delegated to our stub (e.g., internal.acme.example).
- Provide the edge proxy IPs for health checks and SNI (we'll add to the mapping).
- If you prefer Option B, identify the KMS/HSM approach and rotation window you need.

Next steps:
- If we get a decision by EOD Tue (2026-05-18), we'll draft a handoff runbook and schedule a 60-min walkthrough.

Attachments: stubzone-mapping.xlsx (mapping + example records).

Thanks,

Short answers: we prefer Option A (terminate at our edge) unless there's a strong technical reason to shift. We currently manage a wildcard cert in our internal vault, but procurement is prepared to buy a wildcard if needed.

Thanks Taylor / Priyom — quick technical notes to make the tradeoffs concrete. (Attaching mtu-notes.txt with a note about path MTU for the peering.)

Option A (Edge termination):
- DNS: we recommend a split-stub zone where records for *.private.acme.example are CNAMEs to the private endpoint hostname provided by Acme, or A records if you prefer fixed IPs.
- TTL: 300s for failover agility.
- Healthchecks: Redwood will healthcheck the endpoint over TCP+SNI on port 443. If you return 521/5xx we’ll mark unhealthy.
- Certs: Your edge presents the cert; Redwood will not offload TLS in this model. No client certs required.

Option B (Redwood termination / mTLS):
- DNS: create A records pointing to Redwood private load balancer IPs in the stub zone.
- Mutual auth: we'd use client certs for the reverse connection; you'll need to accept our CA or we’ll use one of your accepted intermediate CAs.
- Rotation: recommend 90-day rotation for workload certs; we can support longer windows if you need HSM-backed keys and offline CSR handling.

Operational caveats:
- If you use NAT or port-mapping on your side, ensure SNI is preserved; otherwise we'll see the wrong SNI and routing breaks.
- MTU: encrypted payloads + gRPC can exceed conservative MTU on some peering links; see mtu-notes.txt.

I'll be available in the handoff meeting; happy to draft the DNS resource record examples if you want.

— Karthik
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks — quick proposal: adopt a hybrid approach.

Proposal outline:
- Terminate incoming client TLS at Acme edge (your preferred Option A) so you retain control of external certs.
- Establish mTLS between Acme edge and Redwood's private endpoint for backend calls. This gives mutual authentication and auditability for sensitive traffic.
- DNS: you delegate the stub zone (private.acme.example) to Redwood's resolver for the subhosts we serve; we will only publish A records for the private load balancer IPs (no public exposure).

Pros:
- You keep edge cert hygiene and procurement responsibilities.
- We get authenticated connections and can enforce per-tenant routing + audit logs.
- Minimal changes to your client-facing config.

I can author a short handoff playbook (runbook) for the mTLS bootstrap and certificate exchange; see our playbook link: https://docs.redwood.example.com/playbooks/tls-handshake-handoff

Can we lock a 60-min handoff meeting for Wed 2026-05-20 10:00 PT? If that works I’ll invite people and include a checklist.

— Jonas

Adding compliance items we will need before enabling production traffic for the hybrid model: (see attached cert-rotation-window.csv)

Required artifacts / commitments:
- Certificate rotation policy (frequency, owner, rollback procedure). We usually accept 90d rotation for short-lived certs; if Acme requires 1yr windows we need justification.
- Key custody statement: who holds private keys for server and client certs? If Redwood holds any private keys for the customer, we need KMIP/HSM proof-of-controls.
- Audit logs: TLS connection logs and cert thumbprints must be retained for 1 year for our internal audits. Please confirm retention can be shared or we will provide a sanitized report.
- Vulnerability disclosure: scheduled maintenance windows for cert rotation that may cause brief disconnects; need approval window and on-call contact list.

Please send the items above as attachments or links prior to the handoff meeting. If any of these are blockers, call them out now so we can escalate.

— Laura Bennett
